The lakehouse is a governance decision before it is a technology choice

The lakehouse is not a product; it is a discipline of layers. Bronze keeps the truth as it arrived, silver makes it conform and trustworthy, gold models it for the business — and each promotion is a gated, testable transformation. When the layers blur, you get a swamp; when they hold, you get a platform where a bad feed is quarantined in minutes instead of corrupting a warehouse silently.

Open table formats (Delta/Iceberg) do the heavy lifting: ACID writes, time travel for backfills and audits, schema evolution with enforcement, and storage layouts tuned by measured query patterns rather than folklore.
Below: the failure modes that turn lakehouses into swamps, the reference architecture that keeps layers honest, and the console that keeps storage economics visible.
Four ways lakehouses become swamps
Each failure mode starts as a convenience and compounds into an audit finding — the countermeasures are promotion gates, not policies nobody enforces.

widgets.title: The lakehouse target — click nodes for the migration contract

nodes.label: Unified ingestion
nodes.detail: One ingestion fabric for batch and streams with the schema contracts from the engineering practice — the migration never reintroduces the old point-to-point sprawl.

nodes.label: Open table format
nodes.detail: Delta/Iceberg-class tables on object storage — the format is the exit plan: no proprietary gravity, engines swap without rewriting history.

nodes.label: Catalog & governance
nodes.detail: Unified catalog with lineage, ownership and access policy — the legacy estate's tribal knowledge becomes queryable metadata.

nodes.label: Batch compute
nodes.detail: Declarative transformation on the medallion layers — the tested codebase from the engineering practice, not migrated notebook sprawl.

nodes.label: Streaming compute
nodes.detail: Stateful streaming with checkpointed semantics for the real-time cohort — the boundary with batch is explicit and documented.

nodes.label: BI serving
nodes.detail: Semantic layer and certified marts from the BI practice — consumers cut onto definitions that already agree.

nodes.label: Feature serving
nodes.detail: Feature tables with freshness budgets for the ML estate — the models' inputs migrate with contracts, not with hope.

widgets.note: Click nodes for the contract each layer carries. The open table format is the exit-cost decision — gravity is a choice, and we choose against it.

blocks.x: Table-format defaults — and documented deviations
Defaults favor open table formats with time travel and schema evolution; deviation triggers are written because each one changes what audits can reconstruct later.

blocks.caption: Lakehouse Architecture & Migration: default stack and the conditions under which we deviate
rows: Table format
Delta Lake or Iceberg with schema enforcement
Hive tables only for throwaway zones — no ACID, no time travel
Processing
Spark for heavy transforms; dbt-style SQL for modeled layers
One engine dogma — pick per workload and be honest about why
Streaming ingest
Kafka-class bus into bronze with contract validation
Direct micro-batch without validation — bad rows land silently
Catalog
Unity-class catalog with lineage and ownership
Folder-listing as a catalog — nobody can find or trust anything
Storage layout
Partition/ZOrder tuned by measured query patterns
Partition by date everywhere — it hurts most access patterns
